the conductivity of zirconium phosphate increases with the relative humidity, and that there is a bulk and a surface contribution to the conductivity.

the conductivity enhancement of α-zirconia phosphate in the presence and absence of water vapour, and the effect of bulk hydration.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conductivity of zirconium phosphate at room temperature is due to a mixed contribution of surface and bulk water.
the conductivity of α-Zr(HPO 4 ) 2 is enhanced by water molecules adsorbed on the surface and in the bulk.
, in the temperature range 100–200 °C, the conductivity of α-ZrP is enhanced by both surface and bulk hydration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, at 100°C, the conductivity is dominated by surface water and, at 200°C, it is due to bulk water.
the conductivity of zirconium phosphate is enhanced by the presence both of surface and bulk water.
, at low temperature, the surface and bulk hydration contribute to the overall conductivity in different ways, while at high temperature, the surface hydration becomes the main contribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, at least at 100°C, the surface of α-zirconyl phosphate is highly hydrated, and the conductivity of the material exposed at 2%RH is dominated by the contribution of the surface water, while the bulk water contributes to the overall conductivity only to a minor extent.
α-zirconium phosphates, which have a high surface area, are good candidates as water sensors.
, in the presence of moisture, zirconium phosphate can be considered as an effective proton-conducting electrolyte.
